docstring:
/-- **The orders of birth.** The natural labellings of `c` are exactly the numberings of its
elements by a course from the empty set whose configuration at `c`'s size is of `c`'s kind: on such
a course `c`'s element `i` is the one born at offset `π i`. -/
record_statement: On causal-set growth the present, read as the maximal elements of what a course has born, is a choice of course between bounds defined from precedence: a condition is present at a birth on some course exactly where it is a link (precedence weakly decided), on every course exactly at the one link.
record_law: The orders of birth. Every causal set is grown from the empty set, bearing the element t at offset t with its past (pastIn, pastIn_stem, courseOf, courseOf_grows, courseOf_isomorphic), and the natural labellings are exactly the numberings of its elements by a course from the empty set whose configuration at its size is of its kind (natural_iff_course).
chapter_paragraph: **Theorem** (causal-set growth, and witnesses). *The present on causal-set growth.* The grammar has no relation of presence in time ([Open](#open)); causal-set growth ([07 §2](07-SIGNIFICANCE.md#r-what-can-be-born-next)) is a model in which one can be read and the question asked exactly. Its labels, the order of births, are taken to carry no physical meaning (discrete general covariance, Rideout and Sorkin 2000), a premise of the model. The renumberings of a causal set keeping precedence, its natural labellings (`Presence.NaturalLabelling`), are exactly the orders of birth of the courses from the empty set growing a configuration of its kind (`Presence.natural_iff_course`), and births of unrelated elements commute, and only they (`Presence.rearranges_iff_natural`, an instance of the core's theorem of Mazurkiewicz). What a course has born by a stage is a stem, and every stem with decided membership is what some course bears first (`Presence.born_stem`, `Presence.stem_born_first`). With precedence decided, an element is born before another on every course exactly where it precedes it (`Presence.prec_iff_every`), so what is born no later than an element on every course is its past with itself, the largest relation every course respects (`Presence.past_every_iff`, `Presence.past_largest`); with precedence weakly decided, it is born before it on some course exactly where the two differ and the other does not precede it (`Presence.before_some_iff`), so no order of birth of unrelated elements is common to all courses (`Presence.either_order`). Read the present at a stage as the maximal elements of what a course has born, where the grammar's ending holds on what is born (`Presence.MaximalBorn`, `Presence.maximalBorn_iff_ends`). It is an antichain (`Presence.maximalBorn_unrelated`), and with precedence weakly decided every antichain given by a test is one (`Presence.antichain_present`); two elements are present together on some course exactly where neither precedes the other, precedence weakly decided, and on every course exactly where they have the same future, precedence decided (`Presence.together_some_iff`, `Presence.together_every_iff`), which is not co-presence, mutual reach. A condition is present at the birth of what it conditions where nothing it precedes is born before (`Presence.PresentAt`): on some course exactly where it is a link below it, precedence weakly decided (`Presence.present_some_iff_link`), and on every course exactly where that is the one element it is linked to, with no decision (`Presence.present_every_iff_only_link`). Asked of every causal set, each calibrated decision is exactly its principle: excluded middle for the decided forms of born before, present together and the least element above on every course, weak excluded middle for the theorems on some course (`Presence.every_iff_em`, `Presence.past_every_iff_em`, `Presence.together_every_iff_em`, `Presence.present_least_iff_em`, `Presence.either_order_iff_weakly`, `Presence.present_some_iff_weakly`). On three elements, `0` below `1` and `2`, `0` is present at `2`'s birth on one course and not on another, and the present after two births is exactly `1` on one course and exactly `2` on another (`Presence.Vee.present_swap`, `Presence.Vee.not_present_identity`, `Presence.Vee.maximal_after_two_identity`, `Presence.Vee.maximal_after_two_swap`). On Wüthrich and Callender's four elements their relation, kept by every automorphism, is not what every course has born by a birth, and on those elements it is the past with the pair present together on every course (`Presence.Diamond.kept_not_agreed`, `Presence.Diamond.pastOrPair_iff_together`); elsewhere that join need not be transitive (`Presence.SameFuture.pastOrTogether_not_trans`). Each main theorem is also stated on the courses of the growth themselves, the runs of its process from the empty set (`Presence.every_course_iff`, `Presence.prec_iff_every_course`, `Presence.present_some_course`, `Presence.present_every_course_only_link`). Each theorem is near-definitional, a lemma, a witness or a calibration ([record](../results/records/the-present-on-causal-set-growth.md)).

chapter_paragraph: **Theorem** (any type; claims listed without repetition and compared decidedly, contexts listed). Where each context requires a parity of its claims, a context-free reading exists exactly where no list of the contexts contradicts (claims counted evenly, parities adding to odd). Where m contexts contradict, every context-free assignment, and on average every mixture, meets at most m − 1, while reading each context by an assignment meeting it, one supplied for each, meets all m: Specker (two of three), CHSH (three of four) and Mermin–Peres (five of six) are cases. Lean: `ParitySystem.glues_iff`, `ParitySystem.mixture_le`, `ParitySystem.indexed_met`; [record](../results/records/gluing-under-parity.md). Tsirelson's bound is not stated; the [unity of readings](01-ROOT.md#r-unity-of-readings) is 01's.

/-- Absolute balance is stronger than needed for blindness. The same unaccounted

record_statement: Over finitely many weighted alternatives with a binary target, committed coverage is at most the two error weights plus the weight the evidence separates; for balanced courses of one law, at most the two errors plus the weight within responsive reach, equal to them entirely beyond reach.
record_law: For two courses, not taken as balanced, with the same formations present at every step, alike initial levels on what couples in beyond the part's responsive reach, the rest responding through its couplings, and residual giving and taking alike at every step and condition: every formation beyond that reach is alike through its couplings at every step, and every readout through them up to a step answers alike.
chapter_paragraph: **Theorem** (periphery; finite weighted alternatives, a binary target, complete available inputs; `propext` and `Quot.sound` in some declarations, as the record reports). Committed coverage is at most the two error weights plus the weight the evidence separates. Composed with balanced World courses of one law, the same formations present, alike initial levels of what couples in beyond reach, and answers through everything that couples in up to the answer time, coverage is at most the two errors plus the weight within responsive reach, reach decided, and entirely beyond reach equals them with no decision; common residual exchange suffices for answers alike beyond reach (`FallibleInquiry.alike_with_common_imbalance`), and an omitted exchange can keep correct readouts while invalidating the bound. Lean: `ScientificInquiryNecessity.fallible_inquiry_bound`, `FallibleInquiry.coverage_le_errors_add_reach`, `FallibleInquiry.beyond_reach_coverage_eq_errors`; [record](../results/records/finite-fallible-inquiry-necessity.md). Necessary, not sufficient; structural reach is not time-ordered transmission ([§2](#r-timely-response-necessity)).

docstring:
/-- **Along a run of a frame**, the handed certificate gives new realization within the bound.
Completion-to-realization correspondence stays a visible premise; a bound `B` allows at most
`B + 1` steps. -/
record_statement: Where completion is decided, unfinished steps lower the current rule's certificate, handoffs keep it from rising and completions realize new living content, a run initially certified at most B realizes such content by step B + 1; rules each finishing if kept can, revised every step, never complete.
record_law: Along a run of a frame, with decided completion, an initial certificate at most B, each unfinished step lowering the current rule's certificate, each handoff not raising it, and each completion at step n giving living content realized at step n + 1 and absent before: for some n at most B, such content is realized at step n + 1.
chapter_paragraph: **Theorem** (any process) **and Conditional** (the continuation condition). Along a run of a frame, let each unfinished step lower the current rule's remaining-step certificate, each handoff to a revised rule not raise it, completion be decided and the initial certificate be at most `B`. Then, where each completion corresponds to new living content, the run realizes by step `B + 1` living content absent before (`Handoff.Run.novel_by_handoff`), which under the condition falls under the relevance read from significance (`Handoff.Run.relevance_by_handoff_of_unrestricted`). Witnesses: the realized form is not fixed, and without the handoff hypothesis rules each finishing when kept, revised at every step, never complete (`Handoff.fails_forever`). ([record](../results/records/open-form-realization-under-revision.md))

docstring.astra: “The handed certificate gives new realization within the bound” mentions completion-to-realization correspondence but does not specify or point to decidability, initial rank ≤ B, strict local descent and non-increasing handoff.
